findings.summary: The closed supersession list misses the clause the I05 rule itself cites. W01's in-force base §3 still says both sides 'authenticate exact installed peer artifacts', so it still requires the gate to authenticate the broker's artifact. HS43 neither amends nor lists this clause. The record calls the list closed and the model pins it, so the contradiction now reads as resolved when it is not (Q-HS43-2: 'nothing else is silently superseded').
findings.evidence: architecture/host-interface-inputs/corrected/HOST_INTERFACE_SPEC.md:66-68 (HOST-INTERFACE-DRAFT-001, the pinned base of W01 v2), I05 paragraph: 'Both sides independently load the same verified release/capacity inputs. They authenticate exact installed peer artifacts, manifest/trust custody, PID/start, pidfd, SO_PEERCRED and each SCM_CREDENTIALS frame.' The HS43 effective spec's head (lines 11-16) keeps it in force: 'Everything in the base that is not amended here stays in force.' §7 supersedes only 'base §3 I05 table'. I05 v1-v3 Channel item 2 cites this very clause: '(base §3, §4.3)'. HS43's I05 replacement cites only 'W01 §4.3 as amended by HS43'. H1 (spec 308-309) says the gate 'does not check the broker's artifact'. So the effective W01 design (base plus v2/W02D/HS43) both requires and forbids it. Checked in scratch: the SUPERSEDED tuple has no entry for the corrected base, and check() passes. Required: add the base clause to SUPERSEDED, the record and §12. The replacement keeps the broker's side (the broker authenticates the gate's artifact, manifest/trust custody, PID/start, pidfd, SO_PEERCRED and each SCM_CREDENTIALS frame) and narrows the gate's side to W01 §4.3 as amended (no artifact). The original DRAFT-001 (host-interface-inputs/original/HOST_INTERFACE_SPEC.md:67) has the same text. List it too if superseded versions are listed, as I05 v1 is.

findings.summary: Each I05 contract (v1-v3) then says 'The broker verifies the gate's frames the same way'. Once the gate's list loses 'executable', that sentence by reference drops the executable from the broker's per-frame check of the gate too. HS43 means to keep that check (H1 bullet 1, notAmended[0]), and the list does not record this effect: a silent supersession by reference.
findings.evidence: architecture/i05-gate-channel/README.md:59, i05-gate-channel-v2/README.md:76, i05-gate-channel-v3/README.md:76: 'The broker verifies the gate's frames the same way and treats any deviation as peer failure.' 'The same way' points at Channel item 2, whose clause HS43 replaces with 'the gate verifies the broker's ... not its executable'. amendment.json:391 says 'The broker's qualification of the gate keeps its five checks'. H1 (spec 301-304) says the broker's artifact check reads the gate's exe link. Q-HE2S-7 and Q-HE2S-9 make that read possible on every frame as well. Required: list the three 'same way' sentences with a replacement such as 'the broker verifies the gate's frames by SO_PEERCRED and SCM_CREDENTIALS, pidfd/start, executable (the gate's exe link), label and cgroup (W01 §4.3 as amended by HS43)'. Alternatively, state in the I05 replacement that it changes only the gate's side.

findings.summary: The new race-free start-time sentence is not race-free as written on v6.12. A pidfd from SO_PEERPIDFD or SCM_PIDFD gives no start time by itself. The time comes from /proc/<pid>/stat, opened by PID number, so the number can name a later process unless the gate re-checks the pidfd after the open. The text and both obligations leave out that step.
findings.evidence: From my own knowledge of v6.12. The pidfd API has no start-time query: there is no PIDFD_GET_INFO in v6.12, and the gate has no ioctl anyway. /proc/<n> is reached only by number. If the peer exits and is reaped between taking the pidfd and opening /proc/<n>, n can be reused. The open then names the later process, and the 'reference taken without a race' is that process's start time. H1 (spec 305-307) says the reference is taken 'through a pidfd that names the connected process itself'. O-W03-PEER-EXE says 'read each peer's start time once through that pidfd's process'. O-W03-WRITER-EXE says 'open /proc/<pid> for that process with no PID-reuse window'. None says how. The standard closure: open the /proc/<n> directory, then ppoll the pidfd. No POLLIN means the process has not exited (pidfd_poll reports exit through thread_group_exited), so n still named it. Then keep that directory descriptor for every later frame; it is bound to the struct pid and fails with ESRCH after exit. ppoll, epoll_pwait, getsockopt, recvmsg and openat are already in the gate's v3 allowlist. Required: add that step to H1's sentence and to both obligations, and add a PID-reuse case to O-T04-HS43.

findings.summary: H1 justifies 'not re-measured per frame' by saying that opening the link and FS_IOC_MEASURE_VERITY are not in the gate's allowlist. Only the ioctl is missing. The EFFECT_GATE v3 allowlist admits openat unconditionally, so the gate's filter does allow opening /proc/<pid>/exe.
findings.evidence: architecture/seccomp-allowlists-v3/allowlists.json, EFFECT_GATE duty 'fsync/fdatasync, flock (the durable journal and failure marker)': rule {"name": "openat"} with no condition. EFFECT_GATE has no ioctl. From my own knowledge of v6.12: opening the exe magic link goes through proc_pid_get_link -> proc_fd_access_allowed, the same ptrace-read check as readlinkat. It then opens the executable with the gate's credentials. matrix.json gives READ on planeon_policy_writer_exec_t to ANY_DOMAIN, and the artifact is root 0555, so the open and later reads succeed. Required: say the gate does not issue FS_IOC_MEASURE_VERITY (no ioctl in its allowlist), and that not re-measuring is the owner's choice (Q-HS43-2), not a filter limit.

findings.summary: H1 now depends on Q-HE2S-9 (a): the signed I04 port is 1024 or above and the gate holds no capability. But the §5.3 EFFECT_GATE capability cell, which H2 already edits, still reads 'None, except CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE if the signed I04 port is below 1024'. That is exactly the configuration under which H1's broker read fails, so the effective spec still allows it.
findings.evidence: Spec 436 keeps 'None, except CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE if the signed I04 port is below 1024' (H2 changes only the end of the cell). That is harmless while the kernel capability is not held, but it is residue of the dead branch. Required: have H2 (or a further item citing Q-HE2S-9) replace the branch with 'None (the signed I04 port is 1024 or above, Q-HE2S-9 (a))'. Optionally carry the leftover matrix grant to the queued matrix amendment.

findings.summary: The residual covers only the dumpable writer. HS43 now also writes the gate's dumpability (Q-HE2S-7) into §4.3 as a precondition, and the gate has no capability. So the same uid-0 roles with procAccess on planeon_gate_t (the broker, server and observer) can read the gate's ptrace-gated entries: environ, fd and fdinfo, cwd, root and maps. The gate is the more sensitive process, since it alone reads the two upstream credentials, and that exposure is not stated.
findings.evidence: matrix.json procAccess targets planeon_gate_t from planeon_broker_t, planeon_server_t and planeon_observer_t. Kernel rule from my own knowledge (__ptrace_may_access, cap_ptrace_access_check): a dumpable uid-0 gate with an empty permitted set passes every uid-0 reader's capability-subset test. mem and process_vm_* stay refused (PTRACE_MODE_ATTACH, Yama scope 3). Reopening the credential files through /proc/<gate>/fd/N is still refused by SELinux (credential types: owners only). So the exposure is environ, descriptor names and fdinfo, maps and cwd/root traversal, as for the writer. Required: state a parallel residual (e.g. R-GATE-PROC, citing Q-HE2S-7). Either carry it into O-MATRIX-WRITER-PROCACCESS's evaluation (narrowing procAccess on planeon_gate_t to the broker) or record why it is accepted.

H4 (spec 574): 'the peer-qualification digest of the gate's mutual qualification record (§4.3: the broker's qualification of the gate and the gate's of the broker, which HS43 narrows)'. findings.summary: H3's 'a non-negative directory descriptor' matches HS43-START's 'only with dirfd != AT_FDCWD'. It is a strict subset (bit 31 clear excludes 0xffffff9c in every encoding), and the monitor accepted this direction (SECCOMP-DIRFD-DIRECTION). Two small points remain.
findings.evidence: (a) The acceptance is recorded only in README ('direction accepted 2026-10-15'). It is not among the record's owner decisions or sources, although H3 relies on it; record it for provenance (H3 could cite it). (b) 'which links the gate reads is set by planeon_gate_t's /proc access (procAccess)' is too narrow. procAccess covers only /proc entries of declared domains. A readlinkat with an absolute path reaches any symlink whose type the host policy lets planeon_gate_t read with lnk_file read. Say 'planeon_gate_t's SELinux permissions (for /proc, procAccess)'.

findings.summary: Precision points in the new text.
findings.evidence: From my own knowledge of v6.12. (a) 'runs with uid and gid 0 like the broker' (spec 303-304): the broker's gid is pinned nowhere (§5.3 has only a uid column; O-W03-GROUPS covers supplementary groups). O-W03-PEER-EXE binds the gate's uid/gid, but the broker's fsgid must equal the gate's gids. Add 'the broker's filesystem gid 0'. (b) O-W03-WRITER-EXE: a uid-0 exec recomputes the permitted set as bounding plus inheritable (cap_bprm_creds_from_file). If that exceeds the starter's permitted set, commit_creds makes the writer non-dumpable even with no set-id bit or file capability. 'An exec that changes no credentials' covers this only if read literally; the parenthetical should name it. (c) 'without a hidepid option that hides the peers': hidepid=1 (noaccess) does not hide the entries but still denies access, and hidepid=4 (ptraceable) hides the broker from the gate. Say 'mounted with hidepid=0'. (d) 'which only a maintenance boot may relabel' (spec 314) is true of matrix v4. But the effective spec's own §5.3 HOST_CONTAINMENT row (line 439) still gives planeon_contain_t 'relabel on planeon types' in the enrolled boot. That is a pre-existing inconsistency, now cited, so attribute the sentence to matrix v4 explicitly. (e) R-WRITER-PROC's '(exe, cwd, root, fd, fdinfo, environ, maps)' is not exhaustive (also auxv, io, smaps, pagemap without PFNs); write 'including'. Also 'every uid-0 role' assumes those roles run with gid 0, which is a conservative over-statement.
